reasons: Overlaps on machine learning, robotics, reinforcement learning
subject: few-shot adaptation for aerial segmentation
body:
Hello Professor Finn,

My name is Vinil Polepalli and I am an undergraduate at New York University, pursuing a dual degree in Computer Science at the Courant Institute and Business at Stern. I was a machine learning research intern at the Carnegie Mellon Robotics Institute, where I trained a PyTorch semantic segmentation model to 0.88 mean IoU and 0.94 F1 on 25,000 labeled aerial images and integrated it into an autonomous UAV pipeline running under 100 ms per frame.

I read MAML, and the part I find most useful is that it asks nothing of the architecture: by optimizing for parameters that sit a few gradient steps away from good on any task drawn from the distribution, the same method covers classification, regression and policy learning. The cost that made this concrete for me was those 25,000 labels. They cover one region and one growing season, so a new invasive species or a new site means labeling from scratch, and that is the part of the CMU pipeline that does not scale. What I would want to try is treating each species-site pair as a task and measuring how few labeled tiles a MAML-initialized segmentation model needs to reach the mean IoU we got from the full set, and whether the adapted model still fits inside the UAV's latency budget once adaptation happens on board.

In the past, I have worked on the following related projects:
- Semantic segmentation for UAV-based environmental monitoring at Carnegie Mellon Robotics Institute: 0.88 mean IoU and 0.94 F1 on 25,000 labeled aerial images, sub-100 ms inference across 30 flights
- Hsp90 inhibitor virtual screening in the Chiosis Lab at Memorial Sloan Kettering: 4,566 candidates screened at 0.984 GNN ROC AUC and 5x enrichment, 0 Lipinski violations in the top 50: https://hsp90-dashboard.vercel.app/
- Sole author on cVAE-augmented deep learning for pan-cancer RNA-seq classification, about 98% test accuracy across 5 cancer types on TCGA: https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.02743

I have extensively used PyTorch, OpenCV and Python in past work, but have a lot of coding experience and am adaptable to whichever libraries your lab utilizes. Please let me know if there is a fit in your lab.

I would be happy to elaborate on my skills and where I think I can best help out.

Thank you!

--
Vinil Polepalli
New York University | Class of 2029
B.S. Computer Science (Courant) and B.S. Business (Stern)
vinil.polepalli@gmail.com
